title: The Dog and Its Reflection
text:
A dog had got hold of a fine piece of meat, perhaps from a butcher's shop, and was carrying it home in his mouth to eat in peace. On the way he had to cross a narrow plank laid over a stream.

Halfway across he glanced down at the water. There below him he saw another dog, holding another piece of meat in its jaws, and to his eyes that piece looked twice as big as his own.

He did not stop to think. He wanted that bigger piece, and he meant to take it. He snarled and snapped at the dog in the water, opening his mouth wide to seize the meat.

As soon as his jaws opened, his own piece of meat fell out, splashed into the stream and was carried away by the current. The other dog vanished too, because it had only ever been his own reflection.

The dog stood dripping on the plank with nothing at all, having lost the real meat while grabbing at a shadow.
lesson: Before you chase something that looks bigger, check that it is real and count what you risk to get it. Grasping for more can cost you what you already hold.
